knowledge_point.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector in a Diagram

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096814/assets/ce01bd8db88b289837175407663139e74c6ff845bf1cc2fd1e493d65b5ee0c55-prompt.png)

Consider the picture shown above. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $a$. Choose the unit vector in the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096814/assets/ce01bd8db88b289837175407663139e74c6ff845bf1cc2fd1e493d65b5ee0c55-solution.png)

In $\bigtriangleup AHB$ we have $\angle AHB=90^\circ$, $AH=4$ and $BH=3$. So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\
&= \sqrt{(4)^2+(3)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{16+9} \\
&= 5
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the magnitude of $a$ is $5$. Consequently, the unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= \frac{1}{|a|}\cdot a \\
&= \frac{1}{5}a
\end{aligned}
$$

First, we have to find $m+n$. According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $m+n$ goes from the tail of $m$ to the head of $n$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096814/assets/751e6b9328b65d3c7ed69b609d79416fb2c3cde0d69bf886c016b4fbbce289d7-solution.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}
AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\
&= \sqrt{(\frac{1}{2})^2+(\frac{3}{2})^2} \\
&= \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{9}{4}} \\
&= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the magnitude of $m+n$ is $\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$. Consequently, the unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= \frac{1}{|m+n|}\cdot (m+n) \\
&= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}(m+n)
\end{aligned}
$$
